national-yang-ming-chiao-tung-university.about:
NYCU has campuses in Hsinchu (former Chiao Tung, strong in electronics, computer science, photonics and management) and Taipei (former Yang-Ming, strong in medicine, dentistry and life sciences), plus a Tainan campus. Its alumni underpin Taiwan's semiconductor and electronics industries.

International degree students apply online for September entry with transcripts, study plan, recommendations and TOCFL or TOEFL/IELTS depending on the programme language. Taiwan Scholarships and university awards are available.
national-yang-ming-chiao-tung-university.aid_intl: Taiwan Scholarship (Ministry of Education/Foreign Affairs) and university scholarships for international degree students.
national-yang-ming-chiao-tung-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement (results may strengthen an application). Chinese-taught programmes require Chinese proficiency (TOCFL); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. Selection is by document review (transcripts, study plan, recommendations).
national-yang-ming-chiao-tung-university.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.

rheinische-friedrich-wilhelms-universita.about:
The University of Bonn, founded in 1818, is housed partly in the Baroque Electoral Palace and is one of Germany's Excellence Universities. Its Hausdorff Center for Mathematics and economics department are among Europe's best, and it is also strong in physics and astronomy, agricultural science, medicine and philosophy.

International applicants apply online or via uni-assist, need German C1 for most bachelor's programmes, and pay only a semester contribution.
rheinische-friedrich-wilhelms-universita.aid_intl: No tuition fees at most public German universities; DAAD scholarships and the Deutschlandstipendium (merit, partial) are open to international students.
rheinische-friedrich-wilhelms-universita.tests: No SAT/ACT. Bachelor's programmes are taught mostly in German and require proof of German at C1 level (e.g. DSH-2, TestDaF 4x4, Goethe C2/telc C1 Hochschule). Applicants whose school certificate does not give direct university access in Germany must attend a Studienkolleg and pass the Feststellungsprüfung. Restricted programmes (e.g. medicine) select by grade and tests.
rheinische-friedrich-wilhelms-universita.gpa_note: Open-admission programmes accept all qualified applicants; restricted (NC) programmes rank by converted school grade.
requirements: University entrance qualification recognised in Germany (or Studienkolleg)
German C1 proof (DSH-2 / TestDaF 4x4) for German-taught programmes
uni-assist or university application fee (if applicable)
Blocked account/proof of funds for the German student visa

technical-university-of-darmstadt.about:
TU Darmstadt was founded in 1877 and was the world's first university to establish a chair in electrical engineering. It is one of Germany's TU9 technical universities, with strengths in electrical and information engineering, computer science and cybersecurity (ATHENE centre), mechanical engineering, architecture and materials.

International applicants apply online, need German C1 for most bachelor's programmes, and pay only a semester contribution.
technical-university-of-darmstadt.aid_intl: No tuition fees at most public German universities; DAAD scholarships and the Deutschlandstipendium (merit, partial) are open to international students.

technische-universitat-berlin-tu-berlin.about:
TU Berlin traces its roots to 1770 and has its main campus in Charlottenburg. It is one of Germany's leading technical universities, with strengths in mechanical, electrical, civil and process engineering, computer science, architecture, urban planning and industrial engineering, and close ties to Berlin's startup scene.

International applicants usually apply via uni-assist and need German C1 for most bachelor's programmes; there are no tuition fees, only a semester contribution.

technische-universitat-dresden.about:
TU Dresden, founded in 1828, is a full-spectrum technical university in Saxony and part of the 'Silicon Saxony' microelectronics cluster. It excels in electrical engineering and microelectronics, mechanical and process engineering, materials science, computer science and medicine, and holds German Excellence University status.

International applicants apply online (often via uni-assist), need German C1 for most bachelor's and Diplom programmes, and pay no tuition, only a semester contribution.
technische-universitat-dresden.aid_intl: No tuition fees at most public German universities; DAAD scholarships and the Deutschlandstipendium (merit, partial) are open to international students.

ulsan-national-institute-of-science-and-.about:
UNIST opened in 2009 as a national research university in Ulsan, home to Hyundai and major petrochemical and shipbuilding industries. It teaches all courses in English and is known for energy and battery research, materials science, biomedical engineering, AI and mechanical engineering.

International undergraduates apply online with transcripts, essays and recommendations, followed by interviews; scholarships are widely available.
ulsan-national-institute-of-science-and-.aid_intl: Scholarships for many international undergraduates (UNIST and GKS), often covering tuition.
ulsan-national-institute-of-science-and-.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement stated; selection by document review and interview, with strong maths and science expected. Courses are taught in English, so English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent) is required; minimums are set in UNIST's admission guideline.
ulsan-national-institute-of-science-and-.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.
requirements: Financial documents for the D-2 visa

universitat-hamburg.about:
Universität Hamburg, founded in 1919, is a large comprehensive university and one of Germany's Excellence Universities. It is internationally known for climate and earth-system research, physics (with DESY nearby), economics and business, law, and linguistics.

International applicants apply via the university's online portal or uni-assist, need German C1 for most bachelor's programmes, and pay only a semester contribution, which includes a public-transport ticket.

universiti-kebangsaan-malaysia-ukm.about:
Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia was founded in 1970 to champion Malay as a language of higher learning. Its main campus is in Bangi, south of Kuala Lumpur, with a medical campus in Cheras, and it is strong in medicine, engineering and built environment, social sciences, Islamic studies and environmental science.

International students apply online with pre-university results and English (or Malay) proficiency; programme language should be checked before applying.
universiti-kebangsaan-malaysia-ukm.aid_intl: Limited merit scholarships for international undergraduates; most are self-funded or government-sponsored.
universiti-kebangsaan-malaysia-ukm.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement; admission is based on pre-university results (A-levels, IB, foundation or equivalent). International applicants must show English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL/MUET or equivalent) at the level set by the university and programme; minimum scores not verified.
universiti-kebangsaan-malaysia-ukm.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.
requirements: Documents for the Malaysian student pass (EMGS)

universiti-putra-malaysia-upm.about:
Universiti Putra Malaysia began as an agricultural school in 1931 and is today a broad research university on a large campus in Serdang. It is best known for agriculture, forestry, veterinary medicine, food science and biotechnology, and also offers engineering, computer science, economics and education.

International students apply online with pre-university results and English proficiency evidence; UPM's moderate fees and campus location near Kuala Lumpur make it a popular choice.
universiti-putra-malaysia-upm.aid_intl: Limited merit scholarships for international undergraduates; most are self-funded or government-sponsored.
universiti-putra-malaysia-upm.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement; admission is based on pre-university results (A-levels, IB, foundation or equivalent). International applicants must show English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL/MUET or equivalent) at the level set by the university and programme; minimum scores not verified.
universiti-putra-malaysia-upm.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.
requirements: Documents for the Malaysian student pass (EMGS)

universiti-sains-malaysia-usm.about:
Universiti Sains Malaysia was founded in 1969 and has its main campus in Penang, an engineering campus in Nibong Tebal and a health campus in Kelantan. It offers over 60 undergraduate programmes across natural and applied sciences, engineering, medical and health sciences, arts, humanities, and business and management.

International students apply through USM's international channel with pre-university results and English proficiency evidence. Tuition and living costs in Penang are modest by global standards.
universiti-sains-malaysia-usm.aid_intl: Limited merit scholarships for international undergraduates; most are self-funded or government-sponsored.
universiti-sains-malaysia-usm.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement; admission is based on pre-university results (A-levels, IB, foundation or equivalent). International applicants must show English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL/MUET or equivalent) at the level set by the university and programme; minimum scores not verified.
universiti-sains-malaysia-usm.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.

universiti-teknologi-malaysia.about:
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia traces its roots to 1904 and has its main campus in Skudai, Johor Bahru, plus a Kuala Lumpur campus. It specialises in civil, mechanical, electrical and chemical engineering, computing, architecture and built environment, and science.

International undergraduates apply through UTM's international admission portal with pre-university results and English proficiency (an English preparatory form exists for those below the requirement). Living costs are low, and Singapore is a short trip away.
universiti-teknologi-malaysia.aid_intl: Limited merit scholarships for international undergraduates; most are self-funded or government-sponsored.
universiti-teknologi-malaysia.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement; admission is based on pre-university results (A-levels, IB, foundation or equivalent). International applicants must show English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL/MUET or equivalent) at the level set by the university and programme; minimum scores not verified. UTM offers an English preparatory route for applicants below the requirement.
universiti-teknologi-malaysia.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.

university-of-basel.about:
The University of Basel was founded in 1460 and is closely connected to Basel's pharmaceutical industry (Roche, Novartis). It is known for the Biozentrum life-sciences institute, pharmaceutical sciences, medicine, nanoscience, economics and the humanities.

Applicants with foreign qualifications must meet Swiss recognition criteria and show German proficiency for most bachelor's programmes; medicine requires the national aptitude test.
university-of-basel.aid_intl: Few bachelor's-level scholarships for international students.
university-of-basel.tests: No SAT/ACT. Bachelor's teaching is mainly in German, so German proficiency is required. Foreign school-leaving certificates must meet Swiss recognition criteria (IB Diploma and European Baccalaureate have specific rules). Medicine requires the Swiss aptitude test.
university-of-basel.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.
requirements: Secondary school-leaving certificate meeting Swiss recognition criteria (some need an extra exam)
Proof of proficiency in the teaching language (German/French)
Proof of funds for the Swiss residence permit

university-of-bern.about:
The University of Bern, founded in 1834, is a comprehensive university in the Swiss federal capital with eight faculties. It is known for medicine (with the Inselspital university hospital), veterinary medicine, climate and space research (its instruments have flown on lunar and Mars missions), law, economics and theology.

Applicants with foreign certificates apply by 30 April for the fall semester or 15 December for spring, pay a CHF 150 fee, and need German for bachelor's study. Tuition is CHF 909 per semester, plus a CHF 1,700 surcharge per semester for students who came to Switzerland to study.
university-of-bern.aid_intl: Few scholarships for international bachelor's students; most Swiss excellence scholarships target master's/PhD level.
university-of-bern.tests: No SAT/ACT. Bachelor's teaching is in German (except foreign-language studies), so proof of German is required; some programmes need Latin/Greek. Foreign certificates must meet Swiss recognition criteria. Medicine requires the Swiss aptitude test (EMS) via swissuniversities.
university-of-bern.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.
requirements: Secondary school-leaving certificate meeting Swiss recognition criteria (some need an extra exam)
Proof of proficiency in the teaching language (German/French)
Proof of funds for the Swiss residence permit

university-of-cologne.about:
The University of Cologne was founded in 1388, re-established in 1919, and today enrols around 45,000 students. It is known for its Faculty of Management, Economics and Social Sciences, law, medicine and ageing research (CECAD), and holds Excellence University status.

International applicants apply online or via uni-assist, need German C1 for most bachelor's programmes, and pay only a semester contribution including a regional transport ticket.

university-of-geneva.about:
Founded by John Calvin in 1559, the University of Geneva sits in a city full of UN agencies and NGOs, giving it special strength in international relations, international law, human rights and translation and interpreting. It is also a leader in physics and astronomy (including exoplanet discovery and CERN collaboration) and medicine.

International bachelor's applicants apply online, must meet Swiss recognition criteria for their diploma and demonstrate French proficiency. Tuition is low by international standards.
university-of-geneva.aid_intl: Limited bachelor's-level support; some UNIGE and Geneva-based scholarships exist, mainly for master's students.
university-of-geneva.tests: No SAT/ACT. Bachelor's programmes are taught in French, so French proficiency is required (a French exam may be set for applicants without certified B2/C1). Foreign certificates must meet Swiss recognition criteria. Medicine requires the Swiss aptitude test.
university-of-geneva.gpa_note: Strong secondary or pre-university results are expected; competitive programmes require top grades.
